sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: There's a common complaint, that people don't read books anymore.
sentences.zh: 有一个普遍的抱怨，说人们现在不读书了。

sentences.en: But the truth is, print book sales are up these days.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，纸质书的销量近年来有所上升。

sentences.en: Since 2013, sales of physical books have increased every year.
sentences.zh: 自2013年以来，实体书的销量每年都在增长。

sentences.en: At first, people attributed this to the rise of adult coloring books,
sentences.zh: 起初，人们将其归因于成人填色书的兴起，

sentences.en: but even as their popularity has dwindled, book sales have risen.
sentences.zh: 但即便它们的受欢迎程度已经下降，图书销量仍在上升。

sentences.en: I'm talking about physical, old-fashioned books with paper pages full of words.
sentences.zh: 我指的是那种带有满是文字的纸质页面的传统实体书。

sentences.en: We love them.
sentences.zh: 我们爱它们。

sentences.en: The great Argentinian writer Jorge Luis Borges once said,
sentences.zh: 伟大的阿根廷作家豪尔赫·路易斯·博尔赫斯曾说过：
zh_words: 豪尔赫·路易斯·博尔赫斯

sentences.en: I cannot sleep unless I am surrounded by books.
sentences.zh: 除非被书籍环绕，否则我无法入眠。

sentences.en: And I kind of agree.
sentences.zh: 我有点感同身受。

sentences.en: That's reporter Pierce Gelley, although he's not normally a reporter.
sentences.zh: 那是记者皮尔斯·格利，尽管他通常不是记者。

sentences.en: I'm a graduate student in creative writing, and for the past two years,
sentences.zh: 我是创意写作专业的的研究生，在过去的两年里，

sentences.en: I've taught fiction writing to undergrads at the University of Virginia.
sentences.zh: 我在弗吉尼亚大学向本科生教授小说写作。

sentences.en: I assign a lot of reading, but mostly it's in the form of photocopied pages.
sentences.zh: 我布置了大量的阅读任务，但大多是以复印件的形式。

sentences.en: And don't worry, the print shop pays for the rights.
sentences.zh: 别担心，文印店支付了版权费用。

sentences.en: I don't want to force my students to buy too much,
sentences.zh: 我不想强迫我的学生买太多书，

sentences.en: but I always make sure I assign at least one physical book.
sentences.zh: 但我总是确保至少布置一本实体书。

sentences.en: And I always try to pick something that's beautiful.
sentences.zh: 而且我总是尽量挑选精美的书。

sentences.en: One with a nice font, a lovely page design, a pleasing paper grain, and an intriguing cover.
sentences.zh: 一本字体漂亮、版式可爱、纸张纹理悦目且封面引人入胜的书。

sentences.en: Don't get me wrong, the words inside matter too.
sentences.zh: 别误会我的意思，里面的内容也很重要。

sentences.en: But I think it's important for my students to have an object
sentences.zh: 但我认为，让我的学生拥有这样一件物品很重要：

sentences.en: that accentuates the pleasure of the physical act of reading,
sentences.zh: 它能增强阅读实体行为带来的乐趣，

sentences.en: and something they would hold onto after the class had ended.
sentences.zh: 并且是他们在课程结束后仍会保留的东西。

sentences.en: I personally toss hundreds of pages of radio scripts in the recycling bin every month.
sentences.zh: 我个人每个月都会把几百页的广播稿扔进回收箱。

sentences.en: But I would have a really hard time throwing away a book.
sentences.zh: 但我很难下决心扔掉一本书。

sentences.en: Once the pages have a spine, it's like they have a soul.
sentences.zh: 一旦书页装订成册，它们就像有了灵魂一样。

sentences.en: It would feel wrong, like you're spitting on knowledge itself.
sentences.zh: 扔掉会感觉不对劲，就像是在对知识本身吐口水一样。

sentences.en: It's so hard to get rid of books.
sentences.zh: 要摆脱书籍是如此困难。

sentences.en: This is a story about books, and, brace yourself, how to get rid of them.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于书的故事，做好心理准备，也是关于如何处理掉它们的故事。

sentences.en: And in the words of R.E.M., it starts with an earthquake.
sentences.zh: 用R.E.M.乐队的话来说，一切始于一场地震。

sentences.en: Downtown San Francisco in the background, and we zoom into Candlestick Park.
sentences.zh: 背景是旧金山市中心，镜头拉近到烛台球场。

sentences.en: It was the most Bay Area sporting event imaginable.
sentences.zh: 这是你能想象到的最具有湾区特色的体育赛事。

sentences.en: The Oakland A's were playing the San Francisco Giants in the 1989 World Series.
sentences.zh: 奥克兰运动家队在1989年世界大赛中对阵旧金山巨人队。

sentences.en: Coming into the third game, on October 17th, 1989, the A's were in the lead.
sentences.zh: 进入1989年10月17日的第三场比赛时，运动家队领先。

sentences.en: They had won the first two games.
sentences.zh: 他们赢得了前两场比赛。

sentences.en: Allowing Jose Canseco to score, and he fails to get Dave Parker.
sentences.zh: 允许何塞·坎塞科得分，而他未能阻止戴夫·帕克。

sentences.en: But just as the third game was about to kick off,
sentences.zh: 但就在第三场比赛即将开始之际，

sentences.en: the TV broadcast cut out.
sentences.zh: 电视转播中断了。

sentences.en: When the signal came back, it was no longer a baseball game.
sentences.zh: 当信号恢复时，已经不再是棒球比赛了。

sentences.en: This is Cheryl Jennings in the Channel 7 newsroom.
sentences.zh: 这里是7频道新闻室的谢丽尔·詹宁斯。

sentences.en: As you may have noticed, our power was knocked out.
sentences.zh: 正如你可能已经注意到的，我们的电源中断了。

sentences.en: These were the early minutes of the Loma Prieta earthquake,
sentences.zh: 这是洛马普里塔地震的最初几分钟，

sentences.en: which struck near Santa Cruz.
sentences.zh: 地震震中在圣克鲁斯附近。

sentences.en: This was the first major earthquake ever to be broadcast live on national TV.
sentences.zh: 这是历史上第一次在全美电视直播中播出的重大地震。

sentences.en: We have a report of a person trapped in an elevator in Shelter Bay.
sentences.zh: 我们接到报告称，有人被困在谢尔特湾的一部电梯里。

sentences.en: Part of the Bay Bridge had been destroyed.
sentences.zh: 海湾大桥的一部分被毁了。

sentences.en: There were fires, fallen buildings, widespread power outages.
sentences.zh: 发生了火灾、建筑物倒塌和大规模停电。

sentences.en: In all, there were 63 deaths and almost 4,000 injuries.
sentences.zh: 总共有63人死亡，近4000人受伤。

sentences.en: But this is a story about what happened to the San Francisco Public Library
sentences.zh: 但这是一个关于旧金山公共图书馆的故事，

sentences.en: after this earthquake, and because of this earthquake.
sentences.zh: 发生在这次地震之后，并且是因为这次地震。

sentences.en: The library suffered a lot of damage, especially on the higher floors.
sentences.zh: 图书馆遭受了巨大的破坏，特别是高层。

sentences.en: That's one of the things about an earthquake is
sentences.zh: 关于地震的一点是，

sentences.en: the effect of it is intensified the higher up you go.
sentences.zh: 你所在的位置越高，地震的影响就会被放大。

sentences.en: On the upper levels of the library, floors had caved in.
sentences.zh: 在图书馆的高层，楼层已经塌陷。

sentences.en: Jason Gibbs was a new librarian there,
sentences.zh: 杰森·吉布斯是那里的一名新图书馆员，

sentences.en: but he couldn't go to work for two months after the quake.
sentences.zh: 但在地震后的两个月里，他无法去上班。

sentences.en: It was too dangerous.
sentences.zh: 太危险了。

sentences.en: He says bookshelves had collapsed sideways or fallen on their faces,
sentences.zh: 他说书架侧向倒塌或正面朝下摔倒，

sentences.en: and books lay in piles everywhere.
sentences.zh: 书本散落在各处的堆积物中。

sentences.en: Like the books had been tossed around by some angry force.
sentences.zh: 就像书本被某种愤怒的力量到处乱扔一样。

sentences.en: No one was injured at the San Francisco Public Library,
sentences.zh: 旧金山公共图书馆没有人员受伤，

sentences.en: but the earthquake dumped half a million books on the floor.
sentences.zh: 但地震将五十万册图书倾倒在地上。

sentences.en: Even after two months of repairs,
sentences.zh: 即使经过两个月的修缮，

sentences.en: the post-earthquake situation in the San Francisco Public Library
sentences.zh: 旧金山公共图书馆地震后的情况

sentences.en: was still pretty bad.
sentences.zh: 依然相当糟糕。

sentences.en: Library management determined that the stacks weren't safe
sentences.zh: 图书馆管理层认定书库不安全，

sentences.en: and designated a new room for public browsing.
sentences.zh: 并指定了一个新房间供公众阅览。

sentences.en: Librarians curated a selection of books
sentences.zh: 图书馆员精心挑选了一批书籍，

sentences.en: that they thought the public would most like to read,
sentences.zh: 他们认为公众会最想阅读这些书，

sentences.en: and those books went in that room.
sentences.zh: 这些书就被放进了那个房间。

sentences.en: But they realized along the way that not every book was going to fit.
sentences.zh: 但他们在过程中意识到，并非每一本书都放得下。

sentences.en: In other words, even this winnowed-down selection of books
sentences.zh: 换句话说，即使是这种精简后的藏书选择，

sentences.en: was too large for the available space.
sentences.zh: 对于可用空间来说还是太大了。

sentences.en: They needed to winnow it down even more.
sentences.zh: 他们需要做进一步的筛选。

sentences.en: The earthquake just happened.
sentences.zh: 地震刚刚发生。

sentences.en: And we don't have this shelving anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们再也没有这些书架了。

sentences.en: We need to make space.
sentences.zh: 我们需要腾出空间。

sentences.en: That's a reasonable thing to do if you approach it in a thoughtful way.
sentences.zh: 如果你以深思熟虑的方式来处理，这是一件合理的事情。

sentences.en: Because libraries do get rid of books.
sentences.zh: 因为图书馆确实会处理掉书籍。

sentences.en: All the time.
sentences.zh: 一直都在这样做。

sentences.en: Earthquake or not.
sentences.zh: 不管有没有地震。

sentences.en: Put simply, there are so many new books coming in every day
sentences.zh: 简而言之，每天都有这么多新书涌入，

sentences.en: and only a finite amount of library space.
sentences.zh: 而图书馆的空间是有限的。

sentences.en: The practice of freeing up library space is called weeding.
sentences.zh: 腾出图书馆空间的做法被称为“剔旧”。

sentences.en: If you think about it, it sounds ugly,
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细想想，这个词听起来不太好听，

sentences.en: but it is a really good description.
sentences.zh: 但它确实是一个非常贴切的描述。

sentences.en: That's Sharon McKellar.
sentences.zh: 那是莎伦·麦凯勒。

sentences.en: She supervises teen services at the Oakland Public Library.
sentences.zh: 她负责管理奥克兰公共图书馆的青少年服务。

sentences.en: Avery Truppelman went down the street to visit her and see how she weeds.
sentences.zh: 艾弗里·特鲁普曼走过街去拜访她，看看她是如何进行剔旧的。

sentences.en: You have to weed your garden for, like, the flowers to grow.
sentences.zh: 你必须给花园除草，呃，花儿才能生长。

sentences.en: I'm not a gardener.
sentences.zh: 我可不是园丁。

sentences.en: And weeding is not just about holding the book in your hands
sentences.zh: 而且剔旧不仅仅是手里拿着一本书，

sentences.en: and asking yourself if that book sparks joy.
sentences.zh: 然后问自己这本书是否能点燃喜悦。

sentences.en: There's really, really specific guidelines.
sentences.zh: 这里面有非常非常具体的指导方针。

sentences.en: We're not just randomly grabbing books off the shelf
sentences.zh: 我们不是随机从书架上抓几本书

sentences.en: and putting them in the trash.
sentences.zh: 然后把它们扔进垃圾桶。

sentences.en: McKellar and many other librarians at libraries all over the world
sentences.zh: 麦凯勒和世界各地图书馆的许多其他图书馆员

sentences.en: weed their shelves using the same set of guidelines.
sentences.zh: 都使用同一套指导方针来清理书架。

sentences.en: And it has an excellent acronym.
sentences.zh: 它有一个极好的缩写。

sentences.en: Musty.
sentences.zh: 发霉的。

sentences.en: M-U-S-T-Y.
sentences.zh: M-U-S-T-Y。

sentences.en: M is for misleading.
sentences.zh: M代表误导性（Misleading）。

sentences.en: Or factually inaccurate.
sentences.zh: 或者事实不准确。

sentences.en: U is for ugly.
sentences.zh: U代表丑陋（Ugly）。

sentences.en: This one's a little ugly.
sentences.zh: 这本有点丑。

sentences.en: It's like the cover's a little broken.
sentences.zh: 就像封面有点破损。

sentences.en: Isn't the fact that it's so beat up an indication that it was love?
sentences.zh: 它破旧不堪不正是它曾被爱过的证明吗？

sentences.en: For sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So if it's been checked out in the last three years,
sentences.zh: 所以如果在过去三年里被借阅过，

sentences.en: I'd probably actually buy a new copy of it.
sentences.zh: 我可能真的会买一本新副本。

sentences.en: If it hasn't been checked out in the last three years,
sentences.zh: 如果它在过去三年里没有被借阅过，

sentences.en: I would probably consider it for withdrawal.
sentences.zh: 我可能会考虑将其下架。

sentences.en: S for superseded.
sentences.zh: S代表已被取代（Superseded）。

sentences.en: Buy a new edition or a much better book.
sentences.zh: 购买新版本或一本好得多的书。

sentences.en: This would be like an old manual for Windows 98
sentences.zh: 这就像是Windows 98的旧手册

sentences.en: or an outdated travel guide.
sentences.zh: 或过时的旅游指南。

sentences.en: These are the kinds of books that get shredded.
sentences.zh: 这些都是会被粉碎的书籍。

sentences.en: And the last two letters are T for trivial
sentences.zh: 最后两个字母是代表琐碎的T（Trivial）

sentences.en: and Y for your collection has no use for this book
sentences.zh: 以及代表你的馆藏不需要这本书的Y（Your collection has no use for this book）

sentences.en: because they really want that musty acronym to work.
sentences.zh: 因为他们真的很想让这个“MUSTY”缩写成立。

sentences.en: Those last two, the T and the Y,
sentences.zh: 最后这两个，T和Y，

sentences.en: trivial and your library has no need for this book.
sentences.zh: 琐碎以及你的图书馆不需要这本书。

sentences.en: These are the tricky ones.
sentences.zh: 这些是棘手的。

sentences.en: They're not necessarily statements of fact.
sentences.zh: 它们不一定是事实陈述。

sentences.en: They're judgments of value.
sentences.zh: 它们是价值判断。

sentences.en: What's trivial to me might be very important to you and vice versa.
sentences.zh: 对我来说琐碎的事情对你来说可能非常重要，反之亦然。

sentences.en: But even here, these judgment calls are made by librarians
sentences.zh: 但即便在这里，这些判断也是由图书馆员做出的，

sentences.en: who specialize in the relevant section
sentences.zh: 他们是相关领域的专家，

sentences.en: based on circulation statistics.
sentences.zh: 依据的是流通统计数据。

sentences.en: You just have to trust that your librarians
sentences.zh: 你只需相信你的图书馆员

sentences.en: are doing their best for the public.
sentences.zh: 在为公众尽最大努力。

sentences.en: We want to be able to keep bringing you
sentences.zh: 我们希望能够继续为你带来

sentences.en: the most relevant, most current information.
sentences.zh: 最相关、最新的信息。

sentences.en: And the only way to do that is by having room to do it.
sentences.zh: 而做到这一点的唯一方法就是有空间去做。

sentences.en: So the only way we can do that is by sometimes withdrawing the things
sentences.zh: 所以我们能做到这一点的唯一方法就是有时下架那些

sentences.en: that are not as useful anymore.
sentences.zh: 不再那么有用的东西。

sentences.en: Although some sections, according to the library guidelines,
sentences.zh: 尽管根据图书馆的指导方针，某些部分

sentences.en: are generally self-weeding.
sentences.zh: 通常会自动剔旧。

sentences.en: In other words...
sentences.zh: 换句话说……

sentences.en: They disappear.
sentences.zh: 它们消失了。

sentences.en: Oh, people steal them.
sentences.zh: 哦，人们偷走了它们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Certain sections of the library tend to disappear more than others.
sentences.zh: 图书馆的某些部分往往比其他部分消失得更快。

sentences.en: Books about marijuana, the Bible, and the occult
sentences.zh: 关于大麻、圣经和神秘学的书

sentences.en: are probably the biggest ones I can think of.
sentences.zh: 可能是我能想到的最大的几类。

sentences.en: But for the sections that do have to get weeded,
sentences.zh: 但对于那些确实需要剔旧的部分，

sentences.en: weeding is generally a touchy subject.
sentences.zh: 剔旧通常是一个敏感的话题。

sentences.en: The reason why is probably already clear to you.
sentences.zh: 原因可能你已经很清楚了。

sentences.en: People don't like the idea of books being thrown away.
sentences.zh: 人们并不喜欢书被扔掉这种事。

sentences.en: We like books.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢书。

sentences.en: A lot.
sentences.zh: 非常喜欢。

sentences.en: And perhaps no one loves books more than librarians.
sentences.zh: 也许没有人比图书管理员更热爱书籍了。

sentences.en: There's a part of you that just winces every time you have to remove a book.
sentences.zh: 每当你不得不清理掉一本书时，内心深处总会感到一阵痛苦。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, books are dear to us.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，书对我们来说很珍贵。

sentences.en: Part of my maturing as a librarian is to get over that a little bit.
sentences.zh: 作为一个图书管理员，我成熟的过程之一就是稍微克服一下这种心理。

sentences.en: Yes, weeding is normal and necessary.
sentences.zh: 是的，剔旧是正常且必要的。

sentences.en: But after the 1989 earthquake,
sentences.zh: 但在1989年的地震之后，

sentences.en: the San Francisco Public Library started weeding an unusual amount of books.
sentences.zh: 旧金山公共图书馆开始以异常巨大的数量剔旧图书。

sentences.en: The librarians were told to move quickly,
sentences.zh: 馆长们被要求迅速行动，

sentences.en: and they didn't use musty or any sort of comparable system.
sentences.zh: 而且他们没有使用传统的“麦斯蒂”系统或任何类似的系统。

sentences.en: The librarians were ordered to go through each collection book by book
sentences.zh: 馆长们被下令逐个藏书区、一册接一册地检查，

sentences.en: and insert a slip of paper into each.
sentences.zh: 并在每本书中夹入一张纸条。

sentences.en: Green, yellow, and red.
sentences.zh: 绿色、黄色和红色。

sentences.en: Green meant the book had been checked out that year.
sentences.zh: 绿色意味着这本书当年曾被借阅过。

sentences.en: Yellow meant the book had been checked out in the last two years.
sentences.zh: 黄色意味着这本书在过去两年内被借阅过。

sentences.en: And red meant that it had been over two years
sentences.zh: 而红色则意味着距离某人借阅这本书，

sentences.en: since somebody had checked out that book.
sentences.zh: 已经过去两年多时间了。

sentences.en: And the red books were the ones that were in potential danger.
sentences.zh: 红色的书就是那些处于潜在危险中的书。

sentences.en: Danger because management had decided that the red books had to go.
sentences.zh: 之所以危险，是因为管理层决定必须清理掉这些红色的书。

sentences.en: Compared to the careful consideration of musty,
sentences.zh: 相比于仔细权衡的“麦斯蒂”系统，

sentences.en: the system of the green, yellow, and red cards is a rather blunt instrument.
sentences.zh: 这种红黄绿卡片系统是一种相当生硬的工具。

sentences.en: It's certainly not the only measure whether somebody has borrowed it within the last period of time.
sentences.zh: 它当然不是衡量某人在最近一段时间内是否借阅过的唯一标准。

sentences.en: It felt rather arbitrary.
sentences.zh: 这让人感觉相当随意。

sentences.en: And it wasn't really clear where the red card books were going to go
sentences.zh: 而且并不清楚贴有红卡的图书究竟会被运往何处，

sentences.en: or if they would ever be used again.
sentences.zh: 或者它们是否还会被再次利用。

sentences.en: In Jason Gibbs' department, for example, the art and music collection,
sentences.zh: 以杰森·吉布斯的部门（艺术和音乐收藏部）为例，

sentences.en: the discarded books got sent to an abandoned hospital owned by the city
sentences.zh: 被丢弃的书籍被运到了市属的一家废弃医院，

sentences.en: because there was nowhere else to put them.
sentences.zh: 因为实在没地方放了。

sentences.en: Even battle-hardened librarians like Gibbs felt that the weeding was happening too faSt.
sentences.zh: 像吉布斯这样身经百战的图书管理员也觉得剔旧进展得太快了。

sentences.en: You had librarians in different sections weeding furiously
sentences.zh: 当时不同部门的图书管理员都在疯狂地剔旧，

sentences.en: and not really communicating with each other.
sentences.zh: 彼此之间却并没有进行真正的沟通。

sentences.en: As a consequence, lots and lots of books were removed from the library.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，大量的书籍被移出了图书馆。

sentences.en: And no one quite knew how many, because no one was keeping track.
sentences.zh: 而且没有人确切知道有多少，因为根本没有人做记录。

sentences.en: It was ultimately, I think, a weakness of management from the top.
sentences.zh: 我认为这归根结底是高层管理上的失职。

sentences.en: Jason Gibbs is a pretty even-keeled guy,
sentences.zh: 杰森·吉布斯是个相当沉稳的人，

sentences.en: but that's his diplomatic way of saying that the problems began with the head librarian at that time.
sentences.zh: 但这只是他委婉的说法，意思是问题始于当时的图书馆馆长。

sentences.en: A man named Kenneth Dowlin.
sentences.zh: 一个名叫肯尼斯·多林的男人。

sentences.en: Within a year or two, you could be visiting the public library without leaving your home.
sentences.zh: 用不了几年，你甚至不用离开家就能参观公共图书馆了。

sentences.en: In the years leading up to the 1989 earthquake,
sentences.zh: 在1989年地震发生前的几年里，

sentences.en: the San Francisco Public Library was starting to rethink its whole approach to books
sentences.zh: 旧金山公共图书馆开始重新思考其对图书的整个处理方式，

sentences.en: in light of a new little thing called the internet.
sentences.zh: 起因是一个被称为互联网的新鲜玩意儿。

sentences.en: Imagine plugging a computer like this one into any telephone in the world
sentences.zh: 想象一下，把像这样的电脑接入世界上任何一部电话，

sentences.en: and being able to search any library in the world.
sentences.zh: 就能检索世界上任何一家图书馆。

sentences.en: And a big part of this pivot was when, in 1987, San Francisco hired Kenneth Dowlin as its new city librarian.
sentences.zh: 而这一转型的重要一步发生在1987年，当时旧金山聘请肯尼斯·多林担任新的城市图书馆馆长。

sentences.en: As San Francisco's city librarian,
sentences.zh: 作为旧金山的城市图书馆馆长，

sentences.en: Ken Dowling must make sure that 2 million people have access to 18 million books
sentences.zh: 肯·多林必须确保在有限的预算下，让200万民众能够查阅1800万册图书

sentences.en: and other information on a limited budget.
sentences.zh: 以及其他信息。

sentences.en: Dowling was all about the internet.
sentences.zh: 多林对互联网推崇备至。

sentences.en: He had recently published a book called The Electronic Library,
sentences.zh: 他最近刚出版了一本书，名叫《电子图书馆》，

sentences.en: in which he argued that technology was changing the way people used information
sentences.zh: 他在书中论证道，技术正在改变人们使用信息的方式，

sentences.en: and therefore changing the role of librarians.
sentences.zh: 从而也改变了图书管理员的角色。

sentences.en: This is a clip of him.
sentences.zh: 这是一段关于他的视频片段。

sentences.en: The internet web world, if you will, collapses time, collapses distance, and is collapsing coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，可以说互联网网络世界打破了时间，打破了空间，也正在打破成本。

sentences.en: If this sounds unremarkable, not to mention a bit quaint,
sentences.zh: 如果这听起来很平淡，甚至还有点古雅，

sentences.en: keep in mind that Dowlin was saying all this stuff as early as 1984.
sentences.zh: 请记住，多林早在1984年就已经开始大谈特谈这些了。

sentences.en: He certainly understood, at an early stage, what the internet was going to do for communication.
sentences.zh: 他在早期就确实理解了互联网将为通信带来的变革。

sentences.en: But there was a flip side to Dowlin's visionary concept of digitally networked libraries.
sentences.zh: 但多林关于数字化网络图书馆的富有远见的理念也有其另一面。

sentences.en: Some people felt that Dowlin had a distressing lack of concern for books.
sentences.zh: 有些人觉得多林对书籍表现出了一种令人不安的漠不关心。

sentences.en: There was a sense that when it came to the physical collections, he just didn't have any intereSt.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种感觉，当涉及到实体馆藏时，他根本没有任何兴趣。

sentences.en: Dowlin was also overseeing the design of a new main library for the city of San Francisco,
sentences.zh: 多林当时还在监督旧金山市新总图书馆的设计工作，

sentences.en: which would complete his vision of the library of the future.
sentences.zh: 这将实现他对未来图书馆的宏伟蓝图。

sentences.en: The city is building a new $100 million library that is wired for computers as well as television.
sentences.zh: 这座城市正在建造一座耗资1亿元的新图书馆，里面既配备了电脑线路，也接入了电视网络。

sentences.en: This new library would have twice as much space as the old one.
sentences.zh: 这座新图书馆的空间将是老图书馆的两倍。

sentences.en: But a big chunk of that space wasn't going to be for shelving books.
sentences.zh: 但其中的很大一部分空间并不会用来摆放书架。

sentences.en: Instead, much of the library's interior was devoted to an atrium in the middle of the building,
sentences.zh: 相反，图书馆内部的大部分空间都留给了建筑正中的中庭，

sentences.en: which would rise 86 feet to a conical glass roof.
sentences.zh: 它将拔地而起86英尺，直通一个圆锥形的玻璃屋顶。

sentences.en: Lots of librarians worried that this big, empty atrium wouldn't leave a lot of space for books.
sentences.zh: 许多图书管理员担心，这个巨大且空旷的中庭会占用大量本该属于书籍的空间。

sentences.en: The atrium was evidence that books were not the sole priority of this building.
sentences.zh: 这个中庭就是书籍并非这座建筑唯一首要任务的明证。

sentences.en: And Dowlin wasn't going to let a good crisis go to waste.
sentences.zh: 而多林可不会白白浪费一场好危机。

sentences.en: The earthquake was a perfect excuse to do what he wanted to do anyway.
sentences.zh: 这场地震为他去做他本就想做的事提供了一个完美的借口。

sentences.en: Shrink the physical collection before the move to the new space.
sentences.zh: 在搬进新空间之前，先缩减实体藏书的规模。

sentences.en: Dowlin's administration started sending books to landfills.
sentences.zh: 多林的行政团队开始将书籍运往垃圾填埋场。

sentences.en: In the days after the quake, books are being sent out by the truckload several times a week.
sentences.zh: 在地震发生后的几天里，一卡车一卡车的书每周被运出去好几次。

sentences.en: This is not normal library practice.
sentences.zh: 这绝非正常的图书馆常规做法。

sentences.en: Twenty-seven librarians signed a petition asking Kenneth Dowlin for the weeding to stop.
sentences.zh: 27名图书管理员签署了一份请愿书，要求肯尼斯·多林停止剔旧。

sentences.en: But that didn't work.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有起作用。

sentences.en: So Jason Gibbs and his colleagues decided to do something.
sentences.zh: 于是杰森·吉布斯和他的同事们决定采取行动。

sentences.en: In any institution, you have a variety of people.
sentences.zh: 在任何机构里，你都会遇到形形色色的人。

sentences.en: There are some people who will just kind of do whatever they're told.
sentences.zh: 有些人只会盲目服从上级的任何吩咐。

sentences.en: And then there are other people who feel like they have a higher calling to the profession.
sentences.zh: 而另一些人则觉得他们对这个职业有着更高尚的使命感。

sentences.en: Gibbs and librarians from several other departments felt that higher calling.
sentences.zh: 吉布斯以及来自其他几个部门的图书管理员们就感受到了这种更高尚的使命感。

sentences.en: They banded together and called themselves the guerrilla librarians.
sentences.zh: 他们联合起来，自称为“游击队图书管理员”。

sentences.en: Guerrilla like the freedom fighter.
sentences.zh: 像自由战士那样的游击队员。

sentences.en: Fighting for the freedom to not put little slips of red paper on books.
sentences.zh: 为了争取不用在书上贴红色小纸条的自由而战。

sentences.en: Let's just say that we did not withdraw books because they hadn't circulated.
sentences.zh: 我们不妨这样说，我们没有因为书没有流通就将它们下架。

sentences.en: We generally held on to the collection.
sentences.zh: 我们基本上把这些藏书都保留了下来。

sentences.en: Jason says that other guerrilla librarians snuck into the stacks and replaced red slips with green ones,
sentences.zh: 杰森说，其他游击队图书管理员偷偷溜进书库，用绿纸条替换了红纸条，

sentences.en: thereby designating the book as a circulating book and keeping it in the collection.
sentences.zh: 从而将这些书指定为流通书并把它们留在了馆藏中。

sentences.en: The guerrilla librarians wanted to determine exactly how many books had been weeded and how many had been dumped.
sentences.zh: 游击队图书管理员想要弄清楚到底有多少书被剔旧了，又有多少书被扔掉了。

sentences.en: But nobody had any idea how many books were being taken away.
sentences.zh: 但没有人知道究竟有多少书被拉走了。

sentences.en: And there was a risk that they'd never be able to find out the magnitude of this massive clearing.
sentences.zh: 而且存在这样一种风险：他们可能永远也无法得知这场大规模清理的严重程度。

sentences.en: Because Kenneth Dallin decided to get rid of the physical card catalog,
sentences.zh: 因为肯尼斯·多林决定废除实体卡片目录，

sentences.en: those files full of index cards chronicling each book.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些记录着每一本书的索引卡片的抽屉柜。

sentences.en: The card catalog is an artifact.
sentences.zh: 卡片目录已经成了历史文物。

sentences.en: But I will not support the view that the card catalog is a working technology to help people find books anymore.
sentences.zh: 但我绝不支持这样一种观点：卡片目录依然是一项能帮人们找到书的实用技术。

sentences.en: It is not.
sentences.zh: 它已经不是了。

sentences.en: And most of the libraries in the world know that and have moved on.
sentences.zh: 世界上大多数图书馆都深谙此道并已经向前迈进了。

sentences.en: He was right about this.
sentences.zh: 这一点他确实没说错。

sentences.en: Already at that point, more than 90% of the nation's libraries had computerized their card catalogs.
sentences.zh: 当时，全国90%以上的图书馆已经实现了卡片目录的计算机化。

sentences.en: The earthquake itself allowed the San Francisco Public Library to modernize their catalog.
sentences.zh: 地震本身让旧金山公共图书馆得以实现目录现代化。

sentences.en: With the disaster relief money they were granted, the library was able to get electronic catalog software.
sentences.zh: 凭借获得的救灾资金，图书馆得以购置电子目录软件。

sentences.en: So now, logically, Dallin wanted to get rid of the physical card catalog,
sentences.zh: 因此，从逻辑上讲，多林想要处理掉实体卡片目录，

sentences.en: which the library had stopped updating in 1991.
sentences.zh: 而图书馆在1991年就已经停止更新这套目录了。

sentences.en: San Francisco's old card catalog was not moved to the new library.
sentences.zh: 旧金山旧的卡片目录并没有搬进新图书馆。

sentences.en: It is locked up and inaccessible to the public.
sentences.zh: 它被锁了起来，公众无法触及。

sentences.en: But this move to get rid of the old card catalog caused a surprisingly intense outcry from the guerrilla librarians.
sentences.zh: 但这一废除旧卡片目录的举动却引发了游击队图书管理员们意料之外的强烈抗议。

sentences.en: And it wasn't just a matter of nostalgia or personal preference.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是怀旧或个人偏好的问题。

sentences.en: The physical card catalog said exactly what was in the library before all the arbitrary weeding.
sentences.zh: 实体卡片目录确切地记录了在所有随意的剔旧之前，图书馆里到底有哪些藏书。

sentences.en: If a book was red-tagged and weeded, it wouldn't be registered in the new digital system.
sentences.zh: 如果一本书被贴上红签并剔旧了，它就不会被登记在新的数字系统中。

sentences.en: There would be no record it had ever existed at all.
sentences.zh: 将不会有任何记录证明它曾经存在过。

sentences.en: And so the old card catalog was more than just a card catalog.
sentences.zh: 因此，旧的卡片目录不仅仅是一份卡片目录那么简单。

sentences.en: The card catalog is evidence.
sentences.zh: 卡片目录就是证据。

sentences.en: Evidence of a purge.
sentences.zh: 一场清洗的证据。

sentences.en: To get to the card catalog, the librarians pulled out their secret weapon.
sentences.zh: 为了拿到卡片目录，图书管理员们亮出了他们的秘密武器。

sentences.en: Nicholson Baker.
sentences.zh: 尼科尔森·贝克。

sentences.en: I'm Nicholson Baker, and I am a writer of books, fiction, nonfiction.
sentences.zh: 我是尼科尔森·贝克，我是一名图书作家，涵盖小说和非小说领域。

sentences.en: And I became, for a brief period of time, a library activiSt.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，我成了一名图书馆维权人士。

sentences.en: Baker is a writer of novels and essays that celebrate the minutiae of daily life.
sentences.zh: 贝克是一位擅长颂扬日常生活微小细节的小说家和散文家。

sentences.en: And in 1994, Baker had gotten national attention for a New Yorker article about the disposal of physical card catalogs,
sentences.zh: 在1994年，贝克因《纽约客》上一篇关于处理实体卡片目录的文章而获得全国关注，

sentences.en: a practice that had become increasingly common and which upset Baker a lot.
sentences.zh: 这种做法当时变得越来越普遍，这也让贝克感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: The San Francisco Public Library had a very ornate, beautiful card catalog.
sentences.zh: 旧金山公共图书馆曾拥有一个非常华丽、精美的卡片目录。

sentences.en: That feeling that you have when your fingers would dance over the little cardboard pieces,
sentences.zh: 当你用手指在小纸板上轻轻拂过时，那种感觉，

sentences.en: and you could tell a subject that was popular because the tops were darker.
sentences.zh: 你能从顶部颜色较深看出哪些主题更受欢迎。

sentences.en: There's all sorts of, you know, tricks that were just fun.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这里面有各种各样有趣的小技巧。

sentences.en: The guerrilla librarians reached out to Baker for help.
sentences.zh: 游击队图书管理员向贝克寻求帮助。

sentences.en: By now, it was 1996, and the new library was nearing completion.
sentences.zh: 到这时已经是1996年了，新图书馆即将完工。

sentences.en: The lost books, evidenced only by their locked-away card catalog, were teetering on the edge of disregard.
sentences.zh: 那些遗失的书籍，只能从被锁起来的卡片目录中窥见一斑，正处于被彻底遗忘的边缘。

sentences.en: In their email to Nicholson Baker, the librarians wrote,
sentences.zh: 图书管理员在给尼科尔森·贝克的电子邮件中写道：

sentences.en: You are the only one who can save it now.
sentences.zh: 现在只有你能拯救它了。

sentences.en: Part of me thought, oh God, this is going to get complicated.
sentences.zh: 我内心的一部分心想，天哪，这下可要复杂了。

sentences.en: Oh, it would.
sentences.zh: 噢，确实如此。

sentences.en: At the time, Baker was living just across the bay in Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 当时，贝克就住在海湾对面的伯克利。

sentences.en: So he made a formal request to inspect the card catalog.
sentences.zh: 于是他正式提出申请，要求查验卡片目录。

sentences.en: Never sue anything if you can avoid it, and don't sue a library.
sentences.zh: 能不打官司就别打，也千万别跟图书馆对簿公堂。

sentences.en: This lawsuit took a while, and it was a bit of a mess.
sentences.zh: 这场诉讼持续了一段时间，而且过程有点一团糟。

sentences.en: But it automatically classified the card catalog as a public document.
sentences.zh: 但它自动将卡片目录归类为公开文件。

sentences.en: Now the library had to keep it.
sentences.zh: 现在图书馆不得不把它保留下来了。

sentences.en: And then Baker and the guerrilla librarians got to work in secret.
sentences.zh: 随后，贝克和游击队图书管理员们秘密地行动了起来。

sentences.en: And you know, you can imagine this with kind of Mission Impossible music going.
sentences.zh: 你可以脑补一下伴随着《碟中谍》那种音乐的场景。

sentences.en: Yes, please.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: The guerrilla librarians snuck into off-limits areas in the library.
sentences.zh: 游击队图书管理员偷偷溜进了图书馆里禁止入内的区域。

sentences.en: They took away books that were going to be destroyed.
sentences.zh: 他们把那些即将被销毁的书籍拿走了。

sentences.en: In other words, they stole them.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们把书偷走了。

sentences.en: The guerrillas stockpiled hundreds and hundreds of library discards.
sentences.zh: 这群游击队员囤积了成百上千本被图书馆丢弃的书籍。

sentences.en: In their homes, in their cars, in their offices, in lockers, in boxes.
sentences.zh: 藏在他们的家里、汽车里、办公室里、储物柜里、盒子里。

sentences.en: All in the hope that they would someday be returned to the library.
sentences.zh: 这一切都怀揣着有朝一日能将它们归还给图书馆的希望。

sentences.en: Nicholson Baker stole books, too.
sentences.zh: 尼科尔森·贝克也偷书了。

sentences.en: I was driving back and forth across the Bay Bridge with my car full of books that I had actually found in this place that was the deselection room.
sentences.zh: 我开车在海湾大桥上往返，车里装满了我在那个被称为淘汰室的地方找到的书。

sentences.en: Baker ignored the staff-only signs and walked right into the deselection room.
sentences.zh: 贝克忽略了“仅限员工”的标识，径直走进了淘汰室。

sentences.en: The basement storage.
sentences.zh: 地下室仓库。

sentences.en: All the places where the SFPL were storing books.
sentences.zh: 旧金山公共图书馆存放图书的所有地方。

sentences.en: He picked up a bunch of books that had no match in the online catalog and found some real treasures.
sentences.zh: 他随手拿起了一堆在在线目录中找不到匹配项的书，并发现了一些真正的宝藏。

sentences.en: They had stored all these, you know, including 17th century, very valuable books and stuff was down there.
sentences.zh: 他们把所有这些书，你知道的，包括17世纪非常珍贵的书籍之类的东西都存放在地下。

sentences.en: Baker, along with a historian, began comparing the online catalog to the physical card catalog.
sentences.zh: 贝克和一位历史学家开始将在线目录与实体卡片目录进行比对。

sentences.en: As they cross-referenced the two lists, it turned out that a lot of books were missing.
sentences.zh: 当他们交叉比对这两个列表时，结果发现有很多书不见了。

sentences.en: Way more than anyone had expected.
sentences.zh: 比任何人预期的都要多得多。

sentences.en: Let me tell you, what an opening day celebration today.
sentences.zh: 我跟你说，今天的开馆日庆祝活动真是盛大。

sentences.en: At last, in April of 1996, the new main library opened its doors with panache.
sentences.zh: 终于，在1996年4月，新的总图书馆带着耀眼的光芒开门迎客了。

sentences.en: Talk about fanfare.
sentences.zh: 简直是声势浩大。

sentences.en: Nothing less than a parachute jump into Civic Center with the man holding the symbolic key to the new library.
sentences.zh: 甚至有人手持通往新图书馆的象征性钥匙，从天而降空降到市民中心。

sentences.en: And in May of 1996, about a month after the library opened, the guerrilla librarians organized an event in the library auditorium,
sentences.zh: 而在1996年5月，即图书馆开馆大约一个月后，游击图书馆员们在图书馆礼堂组织了一场活动，

sentences.en: where Baker delivered a speech stating what he had found.
sentences.zh: 贝克在会上发表了演讲，讲述了他的发现。

sentences.en: Baker contended that Dowlin was responsible for a massive destruction of books, the systematic removal to a landfill of at least 200,000 volumes.
sentences.zh: 贝克断言，道林应对大规模的图书毁灭负责，他系统性地将至少20万册图书运往垃圾填埋场。

sentences.en: And I just said it right there in the library itself, in a talk.
sentences.zh: 我当时就在图书馆里的一场演讲中直接指出了这一点。

sentences.en: And I think it really startled people.
sentences.zh: 我想这确实把人们吓了一跳。

sentences.en: The phrase that got Baker the most attention was when he called this mass disposal a, quote, hate crime directed at the paSt.
sentences.zh: 让贝克获得最多关注的那句话是，他将这种大规模处理称为“针对过去的仇恨犯罪”。

sentences.en: This really upset library management.
sentences.zh: 这确实惹恼了图书馆管理层。

sentences.en: And it became this kind of minor dust-up in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 这成了旧金山的一场小型风波。

sentences.en: Word had begun to spread that Baker was writing another story for The New Yorker, one specifically about this whole weeding debacle.
sentences.zh: 有传言称，贝克正在为《纽约客》撰写另一篇报道，专门关于这场轰轰烈烈的清理藏书闹剧。

sentences.en: So the president of the library commission wrote to The New Yorker's editor at that time and attempted to kill the piece by discrediting Baker.
sentences.zh: 于是，图书馆委员会主席写信给当时的《纽约客》编辑，试图通过抹黑贝克来扼杀这篇文章。

sentences.en: It didn't work, and Baker's article came out in October of 1996.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有成功，贝克的文章于1996年10月发表了。

sentences.en: It was called The Author vs. the Library.
sentences.zh: 这篇文章名为《作家对决图书馆》。

sentences.en: A current New Yorker article called it the Great Book Purge, claiming more than 100,000 rare and one-of-a-kind books were hauled to the dump.
sentences.zh: 《纽约客》最近的一篇文章将其称为“大搜书”，声称有超过10万册珍稀和孤本图书被运往垃圾场。

sentences.en: And then things got a little out of hand.
sentences.zh: 然后事情有点失控了。

sentences.en: The library hit back, condemning Baker for accusing them of a hate crime and saying that he misunderstood the problem.
sentences.zh: 图书馆进行了回击，谴责贝克指责他们犯下仇恨犯罪，并称他误解了问题所在。

sentences.en: They also tried to discredit him because of some bad math he had reported.
sentences.zh: 他们还试图利用他报告的一些错误数学数据来抹黑他。

sentences.en: It turns out one of the guerrilla librarians had messed up the measurements of the old library shelves.
sentences.zh: 原来是一名游击图书馆员把旧图书馆书架的尺寸弄错了。

sentences.en: In fact, the new library had much more space for books than the old one.
sentences.zh: 事实上，新图书馆存放图书的空间比旧图书馆大得多。

sentences.en: It was a very bad error.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常严重的错误。

sentences.en: It was very embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 这非常令人尴尬。

sentences.en: Although it didn't change the fact that the library had taken so many books to the dump.
sentences.zh: 尽管这并没有改变图书馆将如此多的书运往垃圾场的事实。

sentences.en: Then both sides started lobbying insults at each other as the local and national press piled on.
sentences.zh: 随后，随着地方和国家媒体的介入，双方开始互相辱骂。

sentences.en: One paper compared Baker to the Unabomber.
sentences.zh: 一家报纸甚至将贝克比作大学炸弹客。

sentences.en: It was basically an analog Twitter feud.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是一场模拟版的推特骂战。

sentences.en: I wasn't prepared to be part of it.
sentences.zh: 我当时并没有准备好卷入其中。

sentences.en: I didn't know that I was getting into that kind of a battle.
sentences.zh: 我不知道自己会陷入那种战斗。

sentences.en: It was really ugly.
sentences.zh: 场面真的很丑陋。

sentences.en: And even from guerrilla librarian Jason Gibbs' standpoint, the whole weeding controversy got a little blown out of proportion.
sentences.zh: 甚至从游击图书馆员杰森·吉布斯的角度来看，整场清理藏书的风波也有点被夸大了。

sentences.en: It probably was not as horrible as Nicholson Baker made it out, but it was horrible enough.
sentences.zh: 它可能没有尼克尔森·贝克所描述的那般可怕，但也够可怕的了。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the new library itself had already been built.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，新图书馆本身已经建好了。

sentences.en: And it was, judging from the influx of visitors, a success.
sentences.zh: 从蜂拥而至的访客来看，它成功了。

sentences.en: As charges and countercharges fly, three times as many visitors stream through the doors of the new library.
sentences.zh: 在指责与反指责满天飞的同时，三倍于以往的访客涌入了新图书馆的大门。

sentences.en: An indication that some book lovers welcome the change.
sentences.zh: 这表明一些书迷对这一变化表示欢迎。

sentences.en: Some of those books saved by the guerrilla librarians in boxes and lockers were transferred back into the collection.
sentences.zh: 那些被游击图书馆员放在箱子和储物柜里保存下来的书籍，有一部分被重新调回了馆藏中。

sentences.en: All the books in Jason Gibbs' department, Art and Music, made it back.
sentences.zh: 杰森·吉布斯所在的艺术与音乐部门的所有书籍都回来了。

sentences.en: But he says that many of the other books didn't.
sentences.zh: 但他表示，许多其他的书却没有。

sentences.en: They stayed gone, and many of them probably got discarded.
sentences.zh: 它们依然下落不明，其中许多可能已经被丢弃了。

sentences.en: Nicholson Baker says he still has some of the books he stockpiled.
sentences.zh: 尼克尔森·贝克表示，他手中仍然保留着一些自己囤积的书籍。

sentences.en: Given the painful experience of the controversy, the library wasn't really interested in reshelving them.
sentences.zh: 鉴于这场风波带来的痛苦经历，图书馆对将它们重新上架并不感兴趣。

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, the controversy wasn't only about what to do with old books.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，这场风波不仅仅是关于如何处理旧书。

sentences.en: It was a debate about what books are.
sentences.zh: 这是一场关于书籍究竟是什么的辩论。

sentences.en: Are they beautiful objects that we can smell and touch and collect?
sentences.zh: 它们是我们能闻到、摸到并收集的美丽物品吗？

sentences.en: Or are they eternal sources of knowledge, accessible to everyone in the ether?
sentences.zh: 还是每个人都可以在网络中获取的永恒知识源泉？

sentences.en: Well, and it's both.
sentences.zh: 嗯，两者皆有。

sentences.en: In a given research quest, you and I might want to find out what is in a book in the fastest possible way.
sentences.zh: 在进行某项研究时，你我都可能希望以最快的方式找出书中的内容。

sentences.en: Well, nowadays, it's miraculous.
sentences.zh: 如今，这简直是个奇迹。

sentences.en: Sometimes you want the words.
sentences.zh: 有时候你想要的是文字。

sentences.en: Sometimes you want more than the words.
sentences.zh: 有时候你想要的不仅仅是文字。

sentences.en: You want the words laid out on the page.
sentences.zh: 你想要排版在纸面上的文字。

sentences.en: Clearly, Nicholson Baker can see Dowland's perspective.
sentences.zh: 显然，尼克尔森·贝克能够理解道林的立场。

sentences.en: But Baker maintains that we shouldn't give up on the printed page.
sentences.zh: 但贝克坚称，我们不应该放弃印刷纸张。

sentences.en: His argument, and the public battle around it in the 90s,
sentences.zh: 他的观点以及90年代围绕它展开的公众论战，

sentences.en: was a big reason why the San Francisco Public Library totally overhauled their collections policies.
sentences.zh: 是旧金山公共图书馆彻底改革其馆藏政策的主要原因。

sentences.en: They made it a policy that if a library branch is considering weeding a last copy of some book,
sentences.zh: 他们制定了一项政策：如果某家图书馆分馆正考虑清理某本书的最后存本，

sentences.en: they must send that copy to a subject specialist, who will decide if it can be weeded or not.
sentences.zh: 他们必须将该副本发送给学科专家，由专家决定是否可以清理。

sentences.en: And for the books that do have to go,
sentences.zh: 而对于那些确实需要被淘汰的书籍，

sentences.en: the San Francisco Public Library developed a community redistribution program
sentences.zh: 旧金山公共图书馆制定了一个社区再分配计划，

sentences.en: to make sure the extra copies of popular books can live on somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 以确保热门书籍的多余副本能够在其他地方延续生命。

sentences.en: We distribute them to schools.
sentences.zh: 我们将它们分发给学校。

sentences.en: And city colleges and prisons.
sentences.zh: 还有城市学院和监狱。

sentences.en: And strangely enough, one of the biggest changes to the modern practice of weeding
sentences.zh: 说来奇怪，现代图书清理工作最大的改变之一，

sentences.en: is something that Kenneth Dowland himself helped establish.
sentences.zh: 竟然是肯尼斯·道林本人帮助建立的成果。

sentences.en: Online communication between libraries.
sentences.zh: 图书馆之间的在线通信。

sentences.en: You know, in an ideal world, you might want to have every book,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在理想世界里，你可能希望拥有每一本书，

sentences.en: but we just don't have the shelf space for every book.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实没有足够的书架空间来放下每一本书。

sentences.en: So you rely on somebody else's shelves to hold the book.
sentences.zh: 所以你得靠别人的书架来存放书籍。

sentences.en: Some libraries spell musty with an I and an E at the end instead of a Y
sentences.zh: 有些图书馆把“musty”（发霉的）这个词结尾的 y 改成 i 和 e，

sentences.en: for misleading, ugly, superseded, trivial, irrelevant, or elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 代表具有误导性、丑陋、已被取代、微不足道、不相关或在别处。

sentences.en: Like if a copy of the book is at another library nearby.
sentences.zh: 比如附近的其他图书馆里有这本书的复本。

sentences.en: Jason Gibbs at the SFPL and Sharon McKellar across the bay at the Oakland Public Library
sentences.zh: 旧金山公共图书馆的杰森·吉布斯和湾区对岸奥克兰公共图书馆的莎朗·麦凯勒

sentences.en: can now communicate with each other instantly
sentences.zh: 现在可以即时互相沟通，

sentences.en: so they can share book space and make different volumes available to readers in both cities.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就可以共享图书空间，并为两座城市的读者提供不同的藏书。

sentences.en: And this has huge implications for what gets weeded and why.
sentences.zh: 这对什么书被清理以及为什么要清理有着巨大的影响。

sentences.en: In this respect, Kenneth Dowland was very right.
sentences.zh: 在这方面，肯尼斯·道林是非常正确的。

sentences.en: He certainly failed in terms of managing the collection,
sentences.zh: 他在管理馆藏方面确实失败了，

sentences.en: but he succeeded to the extent of bringing us into the wider network of libraries online.
sentences.zh: 但在将我们带入更广泛的在线图书馆网络方面，他成功了。

sentences.en: And yet still, because of Baker's 1996 lawsuit,
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，由于贝克在1996年发起的诉讼，

sentences.en: the San Francisco Public Library has kept the old card catalog.
sentences.zh: 旧金山公共图书馆还是保留了旧的卡片目录。

sentences.en: They are legally required to.
sentences.zh: 这是法律规定的要求。

sentences.en: The card catalog was a way of holding onto the memory
sentences.zh: 卡片目录是一种保留记忆的方式，

sentences.en: of a quarter of a million books that they'd gotten rid of.
sentences.zh: 记录着他们清理掉的25万册图书。

sentences.en: Those cabinets full of cards are still there in storage.
sentences.zh: 那些装满卡片的柜子仍然在仓库里。

sentences.en: Practically barricaded in by all kinds of other supplies,
sentences.zh: 几乎被各种其他物资严严实实地 barricaded（隔绝）在里面，

sentences.en: but I'll go down and visit it every now and then.
sentences.zh: 但我每隔一段时间还是会下去探望它们。

sentences.en: Just to say hi?
sentences.zh: 只是去打个招呼？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, just to know it's there.
sentences.zh: 对，好吧，只是为了知道它还在那里。

sentences.en: After this weeding debacle, Nicholson-Baker became even more vested in philosophies and
sentences.zh: 在这场清理藏书的风波之后，尼克尔森·贝克更加致力于档案管理的理念和实践，

sentences.en: practices of archiving and went on to publish a book that touched on all this called Double Fold.
sentences.zh: 并随后出版了一本触及这一切的书，名为《双重折页》。

sentences.en: It looks at these events in the much broader context of the digitization of libraries.
sentences.zh: 它将这些事件置于图书馆数字化这一更广阔的背景中进行审视。

sentences.en: And this book is now commonly assigned in master's programs in library science.
sentences.zh: 这本书现在通常被列为图书馆学硕士课程的指定读物。

sentences.en: We read the Nicholson-Baker book in library school.
sentences.zh: 我们在图书馆学校读过尼克尔森·贝克的书。

sentences.en: That's Sharon McKellar again from the Oakland Public Library.
sentences.zh: 那是来自奥克兰公共图书馆的莎朗·麦凯勒。

sentences.en: She says that the debacle at the San Francisco Public Library has become a case study about weeding.
sentences.zh: 她说，旧金山公共图书馆的风波已经成为了关于图书清理的案例研究。

sentences.en: Why we do weed and how we should weed and what could be done,
sentences.zh: 为什么我们要清理、我们应该如何清理以及可以做些什么，

sentences.en: you know, how to do it well and what to avoid and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如何把它做好、该避免什么以及诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And when it's done well, with care and consideration, weeding isn't so bad at all.
sentences.zh: 当做得好、充满关怀与考量时，清理藏书其实并没有那么糟糕。

sentences.en: For me, weeding is fun.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，清理藏书很有趣。

sentences.en: It's a chance to really touch the books and see how they're doing and see what people are interested in.
sentences.zh: 这是一个真正触摸书籍、看看它们情况如何、了解人们对什么感兴趣的机会。

sentences.en: That's what all this comes down to.
sentences.zh: 这就是这一切的核心所在。

sentences.en: It's what people are interested in.
sentences.zh: 这就是人们感兴趣的东西。

sentences.en: Weeding isn't just about what to cut.
sentences.zh: 清理藏书不仅关乎删减什么。

sentences.en: It's also about what to keep.
sentences.zh: 它也关乎保留什么。

sentences.en: It's about what the public wants to read.
sentences.zh: 它关乎公众想读什么。

sentences.en: Your voice does matter.
sentences.zh: 你的声音确实很重要。

sentences.en: And we're maintaining a collection for the public and for the people who use it.
sentences.zh: 我们正在为公众和使用它的人维护一个馆藏。

sentences.en: And so every time you check out a book from the library,
sentences.zh: 因此，每当你从图书馆借出一本书时，

sentences.en: you are casting a vote to your local librarian roving the stacks
sentences.zh: 你就是在向穿梭于书架间的当地图书馆员投出一票，

sentences.en: to keep this title in circulation for everyone.
sentences.zh: 要求为所有人保留这本藏书的流通权。

sentences.en: That story originally aired in 2019.
sentences.zh: 这个故事最初于2019年播出。

sentences.en: It was reported by Pierce Gelley and edited by Avery Truffelman.
sentences.zh: 由皮尔斯·格利报道，艾弗里·特鲁夫曼剪辑。

sentences.en: Original tech production by Sharif Yusuf.
sentences.zh: 最初的技术制作由谢里夫·优素福负责。

sentences.en: Remixed by Martin Gonzalez.
sentences.zh: 由马丁·冈萨雷斯重新混音。

sentences.en: Ken Dallin did not respond to our interview requests,
sentences.zh: 肯·道林没有回应我们的采访请求，

sentences.en: but a huge thanks to the librarians who helped us with context and background,
sentences.zh: 但非常感谢帮助我们了解背景和内幕的图书馆员们，

sentences.en: especially Shelley Cocking and Mindy Lenetsky,
sentences.zh: 特别是雪莉·科金和明迪·莱内茨基，

sentences.en: both from the San Francisco Public Library.
sentences.zh: 两人都来自旧金山公共图书馆。

sentences.en: Thanks as well to Oren Rodolfsky.
sentences.zh: 同样感谢奥伦·罗多尔夫斯基。

sentences.en: After the break, the dictionary in reverse.
sentences.zh: 休息过后，我们将带来反向词典。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Finding books in the library is now pretty simple.
sentences.zh: 现在在图书馆里找书非常简单。

sentences.en: You can go up to a computer, you type in the name of the book or the author.
sentences.zh: 你可以走到电脑前，输入书名或作者。

sentences.en: The computer will tell you where you can find it in the stacks,
sentences.zh: 电脑会告诉你它在书架上的哪个位置，

sentences.en: if it's checked out or not, how many holds there are,
sentences.zh: 是否已被借出，有多少人预约，

sentences.en: whether the branches might have copies.
sentences.zh: 以及其他分馆是否有藏书。

sentences.en: But before computers, there were card catalogs,
sentences.zh: 但在电脑出现之前，有卡片目录，

sentences.en: massive filing cabinets of index cards.
sentences.zh: 那是存放索引卡片的大型文件柜。

sentences.en: For every book, librarians would have to make a card for the drawers
sentences.zh: 对于每一本书，图书馆员都必须制作一张卡片，放入

sentences.en: that were sorted by title,
sentences.zh: 按书名排序的抽屉里，

sentences.en: and then another card for the drawers that were sorted by author.
sentences.zh: 然后为按作者排序的抽屉制作另一张卡片。

sentences.en: And for nonfiction books,
sentences.zh: 对于非虚构类图书，

sentences.en: a couple more cards for the drawers that were sorted by subject.
sentences.zh: 还需要为按主题排序的抽屉制作更多卡片。

sentences.en: Every time you wanted to sort the information in a new way,
sentences.zh: 每当你想以新的方式对信息进行分类时，

sentences.en: you needed to create an entirely new index.
sentences.zh: 你就需要创建一个全新的索引。

sentences.en: Our senior editor, Delaney Hall,
sentences.zh: 我们的高级编辑德兰尼·霍尔，

sentences.en: has a story about a particularly niche sorting method.
sentences.zh: 有一个关于一个非常小众的分类方法的故事。

sentences.en: So why don't you start with who you are, actually?
sentences.zh: 那么，你先介绍一下你是谁好吗？

sentences.en: Okay, yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: So I am Delaney Hall,
sentences.zh: 我是德兰尼·霍尔，

sentences.en: and I am a producer and senior editor on staff.
sentences.zh: 我是内部的制作人和资深编辑。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So what is your story today?
sentences.zh: 那么你今天带来的是什么故事？

sentences.en: Well, first, I'm going to introduce you to Peter Sekulowski.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，我要向大家介绍彼得·塞库洛夫斯基。

sentences.en: And my levels are okay?
sentences.zh: 我的声音大小可以吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: So I'm not too loud.
sentences.zh: 所以我声音不会太大。

sentences.en: I try to not pop my Ps, but I get excited.
sentences.zh: 我尽量不让爆破音太重，但我一兴奋就会这样。

sentences.en: I'll try not to talk too faSt.
sentences.zh: 我会尽量语速不要太快。

sentences.en: And the stuff that Peter gets really excited about,
